title: add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: customers with mixed-region deployments required deterministic KMS routing while preserving auditable, append-only commitments for cross-region fallback. This PR introduces a lightweight per-tenant residency assertor, an operator-configurable KMS operator allowlist, and an "audit commitment gateway" that signs short commitment records for any request that is routed off-region or to a fallback key.

What it does: Adds a residency assertor that derives a tenant region preference from (in order) tenant metadata, residency claim headers, and recent routing history (sticky hints). When explicit tenancy region is missing, the assertor emits a deterministic candidate list rather than a single decision to enable safe canary rollouts. KMS selection now consults an allowlist and a staged preference table; if the chosen KMS is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and forwarded through the audit commitment gateway, which atomically records a signed commitment (SHA256 -> operator KMS sign) and returns a short commitment id that is stored in the request audit trail.

Rollout plan: feature is gated behind feature flag "residency_assertor_v1" with three rollout modes: disabled, observe-only (assertions emitted to audit but not enforced), and enforce. We will start in observe-only across a small percentage of traffic, then flip to enforce for specific enterprise tenants. Backwards compatible: if not enabled, runtime behavior is unchanged.

Configuration: new Helm values documented under deploy/helm/redwood-private/values-residency.yaml. Operators can configure: operator_kms_allowlist (ARNs), fallback_policy (prefer-nearest|prefer-cost|consent-first), commit_signer_key (service principal), and audit_holdback_window_seconds (short buffer window used by commitment gateway for transient redaction requests).

Security and compliance notes: commitments are signed by a dedicated signing key stored in the operator KMS; commitments include a compact mutation-proof vector (timestamp + request-hash + origin-region) to support later non-repudiable verification. Audit-forwarder retains commitment IDs and can fetch the signed commitment for external compliance queries. Access to the commitment verification endpoint is RBAC-protected via a new v2 policy template.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for deterministic candidate ordering, a simulation harness to exercise cross-region fallback under random failure, and an integration test that verifies the signed commitment roundtrip against the operator KMS emulator. Performance overhead measured at ~0.6ms median added latency in observe-only mode, 1.8ms in enforce mode for off-region fallbacks.

Migration / Operational guidance: operators should seed operator_kms_allowlist before enabling enforce mode; enable observe-only for 72 hours and review audit commitments using the console (Audit -> Commitments view). We include a small migration script to backfill missing residency hints from a 30-day routing history.

Related: Linked Linear ENG-4123 (residency policy), PM-982 (enterprise residency product work). Addresses support ticket SUP-2345 about inconsistent KMS selection for EU-regulated tenants.

release_notes:
- Introduce Residency Assertor for deterministic tenant-region recommendations.
- Add Audit Commitment Gateway for signed, non-repudiable records when requests are routed off-region.
- New operator KMS allowlist and selection policy.
- Helm values for residency and migration backfill script.

Operators: enable via feature flag residency_assertor_v1 and follow the observe-only rollout documented in docs/security/kms-residency.md.
